title: Free Starter Pack
description: 15 beginner and intermediate pump operator scenarios included with FirePumpSim.

problems.title: Set PDP for 200′ 1¾″
problems.question: Engine 181 is pumping a 200 ft 1¾-inch attack line with a ChiefXD 185 nozzle flowing 185 GPM at 50 PSI. Use C = 15.5. No elevation or appliance loss. What pump discharge pressure should be set?
problems.instructorExplanation: Calculate hose friction loss and add nozzle pressure.
problems.explainMistake: Do not use nozzle pressure alone; the pump must also overcome hose friction loss.

problems.title: Set PDP for 300′ 1¾″
problems.question: Engine 181 is pumping a 300 ft 1¾-inch attack line with a ChiefXD 185 nozzle flowing 185 GPM at 50 PSI. Use C = 15.5. No elevation or appliance loss. What pump discharge pressure should be set?
problems.instructorExplanation: The extra hose length increases friction loss compared with a 200-ft stretch.

problems.title: Set PDP for 200′ 2″
problems.question: Engine 181 is pumping a 200 ft 2-inch attack line with a ChiefXD 265 nozzle flowing 265 GPM at 50 PSI. Use C = 8. No elevation or appliance loss. What pump discharge pressure should be set?
problems.instructorExplanation: Use the stated 2-inch coefficient, not the 1¾-inch coefficient.
problems.explainMistake: Using the wrong hose coefficient changes the friction loss significantly.

problems.title: Set PDP for 2½ Smooth Bore
problems.question: Engine 181 is pumping 200 ft of 2½-inch hose to a 1⅛-inch smooth bore flowing 265 GPM at 50 PSI. Use C = 2. No elevation or appliance loss. What pump discharge pressure should be set?
problems.instructorExplanation: Add the 50 PSI smooth-bore nozzle pressure to the 2½-inch hose friction loss.
problems.explainMistake: No appliance loss is stated in this problem.

problems.title: Set PDP for 3rd Floor Line
problems.question: Engine 181 is pumping a 200 ft 1¾-inch attack line with a ChiefXD 185 nozzle to the 3rd floor. The nozzle flows 185 GPM at 50 PSI. For this training problem, use height = (floor number - 1) × 10 ft and 0.5 PSI/ft for elevation. What pump discharge pressure should be set?
problems.instructorExplanation: The 0.5 PSI/ft value is an explicit fireground training approximation for this question.
problems.explainMistake: Do not count three full 10-ft floors above grade; the first floor is treated as grade level.

nozzles: Two ChiefXD 185 fog nozzles, 185 GPM @ 50 PSI each

problems.title: Set PDP for Wye Operation
problems.question: Engine 181 is pumping 200 ft of 2½-inch hose to a wye. Branch A is 150 ft of 1¾-inch hose and Branch B is 200 ft of 1¾-inch hose. Both nozzles flow 185 GPM at 50 PSI. Add the scenario-stated 10 PSI wye loss. What pump discharge pressure should be set for the governing branch?
formulaBreakdown: Branch A FL ≈ 80 PSI; Branch B FL ≈ 106 PSI.
problems.instructorExplanation: Use total flow in the common line, then the loss in the governing branch.
problems.explainMistake: Do not add both branch friction losses together; only the governing flow path sets pressure.

problems.title: Set PDP for Siamese Supply
problems.question: Engine 181 is supplying a siamese with two equal 200 ft 2½-inch lines feeding a 500 GPM master stream at 80 PSI. Split flow evenly and add the scenario-stated 10 PSI siamese loss. What pump discharge pressure should be set?
problems.instructorExplanation: Parallel equal lines split the flow; use one line's friction loss in the pressure path.
problems.explainMistake: Do not calculate each line at the full 500 GPM.

hoses: Two 200′ 2½″ supply lines to portable monitor

problems.title: Set PDP for Portable Monitor
problems.question: Engine 181 is supplying a portable monitor with two equal 200 ft 2½-inch lines. The monitor flows 500 GPM total at 80 PSI. Split the flow evenly. This problem states no additional appliance loss. What pump discharge pressure should be set?
problems.instructorExplanation: This is a simplified training scenario with no separate monitor-loss value assigned.
problems.explainMistake: Do not add the two parallel line friction losses together.

problems.title: Set PDP for 3rd Floor Standpipe
problems.question: Engine 181 is supplying a 3rd-floor standpipe attack. The crew has 150 ft of 2½-inch hose from the outlet to a 1⅛-inch smooth bore flowing 265 GPM at 50 PSI. Use the stated 10 PSI elevation allowance and assume 25 PSI standpipe/FDC system loss for this scenario. What pump discharge pressure should be set?
problems.instructorExplanation: The 25 PSI system loss is an explicit scenario assumption, not a universal standpipe value.
problems.explainMistake: Include hose loss, nozzle pressure, the stated elevation allowance, and stated system loss.

problems.title: Set PDP for FDC Standpipe
problems.question: Engine 181 is pumping the FDC for a 4th-floor standpipe attack. The crew has 200 ft of 2½-inch hose from the outlet to a 1⅛-inch smooth bore flowing 265 GPM at 50 PSI. Use the stated 15 PSI elevation allowance and assume 25 PSI FDC/standpipe system loss for this scenario. What pump discharge pressure should be set?
problems.instructorExplanation: The 25 PSI system loss is explicitly assigned by this scenario.
problems.explainMistake: Do not treat the scenario's 25 PSI system loss as a universal value outside this problem.

problems.title: Set PDP for Sprinkler Support
problems.question: For this training scenario, the sprinkler system flowing GPM is unknown. Do not calculate hose friction loss from an assumed flow. Use the stated 150 PSI sprinkler-support base plus a stated 25 PSI FDC allowance. What pump discharge pressure should be set?
problems.instructorExplanation: The 150 + 25 values are stated training assumptions, not universal values for every sprinkler system.
problems.explainMistake: Do not invent a sprinkler flow when the problem gives none.

problems.title: Set PDP for Relay Supply
problems.question: Engine 181 is the relay supply engine pumping 800 ft of 5-inch LDH to a receiving engine. The relay flow is 1000 GPM and the receiving engine needs 20 PSI intake pressure. Use C = 0.08. What discharge pressure should Engine 181 set?
problems.instructorExplanation: Overcome relay-line friction loss while maintaining the stated receiving-engine intake pressure.
problems.explainMistake: Do not stop at the 64 PSI hose friction loss.

problems.title: Find Hydrant Pressure Drop Percentage
problems.question: Engine 181 is flowing 1000 GPM from a hydrant. Static pressure was 70 PSI and residual pressure is 50 PSI while flowing. Use pressure drop % = (static - residual) ÷ static × 100. What is the hydrant pressure-drop percentage?
problems.instructorExplanation: The original question asked for a percentage, so the correct answer is 28.6%, not the raw 20 PSI pressure difference.
problems.explainMistake: 20 PSI is the pressure difference; divide by the 70 PSI static pressure and multiply by 100 to answer the percentage question.

problems.title: Calculate Nozzle Reaction
problems.question: A crew is operating a 1⅛-inch smooth bore handline at 50 PSI nozzle pressure. Use NR = 1.57 × diameter² × NP. What is the approximate nozzle reaction in pounds?
problems.instructorExplanation: Square the tip diameter, then multiply by nozzle pressure and 1.57.
problems.explainMistake: Do not forget to square the smooth-bore tip diameter.

nozzles: Deck gun 1½″ smooth bore tip at 80 PSI
sceneElements.elevation: Mounted on apparatus; no elevation component in this flow-only question

problems.title: Calculate Deck Gun Flow
problems.question: Engine 181 is using the deck gun with a 1½-inch smooth bore tip at 80 PSI nozzle pressure. Use GPM = 29.7 × diameter² × √NP. What is the approximate flow?
problems.instructorExplanation: This is a flow question, not a pump-pressure question.
problems.explainMistake: Do not answer 80; 80 PSI is nozzle pressure, not GPM.
